title: A real plan runs end to end on the graph engine
description: The exit criterion of the viability work: prove that PgeEngine executing the committed 29 KB spec and its 14 contracts produces no StateBloatError, leaves state.spec non-null, and terminates at a declared terminal node. Note the terminal will NOT be the finalize node -- under the shipped autopilot noop mechanism the git-effect commit node is still refused FAIL_CLOSED, and reaching finalize needs a durable mechanism that is out of scope here.

successCriteria.description: A committed test runs PgeEngine over the committed artifact with the real 29,247-byte spec and its 14 contracts and asserts zero failures with errorClass StateBloatError.
The same run leaves state.spec non-null and state.sprintContracts holding all 14 contracts.

The run terminates at a node the artifact declares, and the test names which one and why -- explicitly recording that it is not `finalize` and that the commit refusal under the noop mechanism is the reason.
The sprint-1 measurement artifact is regenerated and its diff shows the rejections gone, so the fix is evidenced by the same instrument that found the defect.
docs/pge-graph.md records that the graph engine has been run against a real workload, with the payload sizes and the terminal reached, replacing any claim that rests only on fixtures.
Full suite, typecheck, typecheck:tests, lint and build are green.

nonGoals: Reaching the finalize node, or changing the checkpoint mechanism to reach it.
Making the run report failure correctly -- that is sprint 5.
stopConditions: The run still rejects writes after the cap change -- stop and report which channel, since it means the corpus missed a payload shape.
Reaching a declared terminal requires editing a node body -- stop and report rather than widening the sprint.
definitionOfDone: All required criteria met, the full suite plus typecheck, typecheck:tests, lint and build are green, and every documentation claim added is backed by a test that fails when the claim stops being true.
generatorNotes: This is the payoff sprint for sprints 1-3 and it should reuse their harness rather than build a third one. Be precise in the assertions about WHICH terminal is reached: PgeEngine.run always calls commit.finalize (the boundary METHOD, :476-483) regardless of whether the graph's finalize NODE executed, and those two are different things -- the node's only edge in is commit -> finalize and commit is refused. Conflating them will produce a test that asserts something false. If state.spec is non-null but commit.finalize still throws, that is sprint 7's defect appearing early: record it and do not paper over it.
evaluatorNotes: The failure mode to hunt is a test that passes because it ran a smaller spec. Measure the spec's byte size inside the test and assert it. Confirm all 14 contracts landed rather than a subset -- a partial write would still satisfy a naive non-null check. Verify sc-4-3 names the real terminal by reading the run's spans yourself rather than trusting the assertion's label. Verify the regenerated measurement in sc-4-4 is genuinely regenerated, by diffing it against the sprint-1 version.
